statement: Let f : X → Z be a projective contraction between normal irreducible compact Kähler spaces. Suppose that (X, B + M) has globally modified-big total boundary and that A = [KX + B + MX] = f∗ γ, γ ∈ H1,1 BC(Z). There is an adjoint-preserving preparation as in Lemma 3.29, with multiplier ideal J1 ⊇ Jo, for which Ri f∗J1 = 0 (i > 0), f∗ON1 = OZ/(f∗J1), N1 = V (J1). (3.18) If N1 dominates Z, then f∗J1 = 0. Otherwise there are generalized data (Z, BZ + N), a projective carrier τ : T → Z with T smooth and compact Kähler, a real SNC structure divisor CT , and a Kähler class βT such that [KZ + BZ + NZ] = γ, τ∗ γ = [KT + CT ] + βT , NT = βT , BZ = τ∗CT ≥ 0, BZ + NZ is globally modified big. (3.19) The negative components of CT are τ-exceptional, and JZ := J (Z, BZ + N) = τ∗OT (−⌊CT ⌋) ⊇ f∗J1. (3.20) In particular the base data are gklt wherever f∗J1 is the unit ideal. If the source data are gklt, the base data are gklt. All adjoint identities are preserved by pullback to higher models.
